Together, this might have led to an underestimation of the presence of the large cribriform pattern in the current study. Furthermore, treatment modalities have been modified over the years with more common use of active surveillance in low-risk patients who received active treatment two decades ago. This threshold is easy to apply, but is subjective. Furthermore, interobserver variability on assessment of the cribriform pattern could also affect the outcome of different studies. map_chunks.summary_text: This chunk reports findings from a large cohort study (n=1,887; median follow-up 13.4 years) from the European Randomised Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer [S3, S5|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17550]. Invasive cribriform and IDC patterns are established as adverse prognostic features in prostate cancer [S1]. The large cribriform pattern was specifically defined as glands at least twice the size of adjacent benign glands [S4]. Any cribriform pattern was detected in 280/1,887 men, with prevalence rising steeply from GG1 (1.1%) to GG5 (59.3%); the large cribriform pattern was absent in GG1 and increased to 18.1% in GG4 [S7]. In multivariable Cox regression analyses, both small and large cribriform patterns were independently associated with significantly worse MFS (small: HR=3.04; large: HR=3.17) and DSS (small: HR=4.07; large: HR=4.13), all P<0.005 [S8]. Critically, no statistically significant difference in MFS (P=0.77) or DSS (P=0.96) was found between the large and small cribriform patterns [S9], challenging the assumption that large cribriform morphology confers worse prognosis than small cribriform on biopsy.

map_chunks.summary_text: This chunk summarises key histopathological and prognostic features of Gleason score 7 prostate cancer and its subpatterns [S1|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17555]. Gleason pattern 4 is categorised into four growth subtypes: poorly formed, fused, glomeruloid, and cribriform [S2|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17555]. Multiple studies demonstrate that the invasive cribriform pattern is independently associated with worse BCRFS, MFS, and DSS compared to non-cribriform architecture, in both biopsies and radical prostatectomy specimens [S3|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17555]. Intraductal carcinoma (IDC) is defined as malignant epithelial proliferation confined to distended acini/prostatic ducts, typically co-existing with invasive carcinoma [S3|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17555]. Both IDC and invasive cribriform carcinoma are adverse prognostic factors that significantly improve prediction model performance [S4|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17555]. Consequently, the 2019 ISUP consensus and GUPS recommend mandatory reporting of invasive cribriform and IDC in all prostate cancer pathology reports [S5|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17555].

findings.claim: Cribriform pattern definition: Iczkowski et al. required >12 luminal spaces in a cribriform structure
findings.verbatim_support: Because the reporting of cribriform architecture is important for clinical decision-making, details on the definition of cribriform pattern and its distinction from potential mimickers are coming to attention. In earlier studies, different-sized thresholds have been used for cribriform pattern definition. For instance, Iczkowski et al. required the presence of more than 12 luminal spaces in a cribriform structure, while Trudel et al. included lesions exceeding the size of an average benign gland and Van Leenders et al. did not set a specific size limitation. Furthermore, Hollemans et al. found that grade group 2 patients with large cribriform structures exceeding twice the size of adjacent benign glands at radical prostatectomy had shorter BCRFS than men with small cribriform glands. It is currently unknown whether large cribriform structures at diagnostic biopsies are also associated with worse outcome compared to small cribriform glands. The objective of the current study is to determine whether large cribriform structures have independent adverse predictive value for clinical outcome compared to small cribriform architecture in a large cohort of prostate cancer biopsies with long-term follow-up.

map_chunks.summary_text: This chunk introduces the clinical relevance of cribriform architecture in prostate cancer and the heterogeneity in its histological definition across studies [S1|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17556]. Three distinct size-based definitional thresholds have been applied historically: Iczkowski et al. required >12 luminal spaces, Trudel et al. required lesion size exceeding that of an average benign gland, and Van Leenders et al. imposed no size limitation [S3|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17556]. Hollemans et al. demonstrated that grade group 2 patients with large cribriform structures (>2× the size of adjacent benign glands) at radical prostatectomy had shorter biochemical recurrence-free survival (BCRFS) compared to those with small cribriform glands [S4|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17556]. Whether this size-dependent prognostic difference extends to diagnostic biopsies remains unknown [S5|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17556], motivating the current study to evaluate large versus small cribriform architecture as an independent predictor of clinical outcome in a large biopsy cohort with long-term follow-up [S6|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17556].

findings.claim: Large cribriform pattern defined as diameter ≥2x the size of adjacent benign glands
findings.verbatim_support: All biopsies were revised by one senior pathologist (G.v.L.) together with a combination of four junior (C.K., I.K., L.R., T.H.) pathologists, who each reviewed a subset of the cases. In case of discordances, the senior pathologist's assessment was recorded. The observers were all blinded to clinical information and patient outcome. For each biopsy we recorded tumour length in millimetres, highest Gleason score/grade group according to the 2014 ISUP recommendations and the presence of invasive cribriform and intraductal carcinoma. Cribriform carcinoma was defined as a contiguous proliferation of malignant epithelial cells with the majority of tumour cells not being in contact with adjacent stroma and with identifiable intercellular lumina. A large cribriform pattern was defined as having a diameter of at least twice the size of adjacent benign glands, while the diameter of a small cribriform pattern was smaller than twice the size of pre-existing benign glands (Figure 1). IDC was distinguished from highgrade prostate intra-epithelial neoplasia (HGPIN) by morphological features as described by Guo et al., and not incorporated into the grade group assessment. Because their considerable morphological overlap requires basal cell immunohistochemistry for differentiation, invasive cribriform and intraductal carcinoma were analysed as one group (invCR/IDC). If a case had both large and small invCR/IDC, it was classified as large cribriform in further analysis.

Cribriform carcinoma is defined as a contiguous proliferation of malignant epithelial cells, the majority not in contact with adjacent stroma, with identifiable intercellular lumina [S5]. Large cribriform pattern is defined as diameter ≥2x adjacent benign glands, while small cribriform pattern is diameter <2x [S6]. IDC is distinguished from HGPIN by morphological criteria per Guo et al. and is excluded from grade group assignment [S7]. Because invasive cribriform carcinoma and IDC share considerable morphological overlap requiring basal cell IHC for definitive differentiation, they were grouped together as invCR/IDC [S8]. When both large and small invCR/IDC co-existed, the case was classified as large cribriform [S9]. Per biopsy, tumour length (mm), highest Gleason score/grade group (2014 ISUP), and presence of invCR/IDC were recorded [S4].

findings.claim: Cribriform architecture defined as: contiguous epithelial proliferation where majority of tumour cells do not contact adjacent stroma, with visible intercellular lumina (ISUP consensus, no minimal size criterion)
findings.verbatim_support: Slightly different criteria for cribriform architecture have been used in various publications, particularly with regard to a minimal size threshold. In a recent ISUP panel meeting, it was consented that cribriform architecture consisted of a contiguous epithelial proliferation in which the majority of tumour cells does not contact adjacent stroma and with visible intercellular lumina. map_chunks.summary_text: This chunk (PMC9321809) compares the prognostic significance of large versus small cribriform patterns in grade group 2 prostate cancer. Multivariable analysis (Hollemans et al., radical prostatectomy cohort) showed large cribriform pattern was the only significant predictor of BCRFS, while small cribriform pattern lost significance [S2]. However, a biopsy study (Flood et al.) using a threshold of ≤12 vs >12 punched-out lumina found both small and large cribriform patterns significantly associated with upgrading and extraprostatic expansion at subsequent radical prostatectomy [S4]. Recognition of large cribriform pattern on biopsy is hypothesised to be hampered by sampling artefacts [S3]. Clinically, cribriform carcinoma at radical prostatectomy is associated with higher PiRADS scores on MRI [S6]. Three commercially available companion diagnostics for aggressive grade group 2 disease have been partly shown to reflect cribriform morphology [S7], underscoring the value of multimodal risk stratification [S5].

findings.claim: Large cribriform architecture believed to have worse outcome than small cribriform pattern
findings.verbatim_support: The strength of this study is the use of a large well-characterised prostate biopsy cohort with longterm clinical follow-up of more than 13 years. This allows for the analysis of detailed pathological features with strong and relevant clinical endpoints such as occurrence of metastasis and disease-specific death. One inherent disadvantage of the use of samples with such long-term follow-up is that, at that time, stateof-the-art clinical practice was different from the present. In the 1990s standard sextant biopsies were used, while current biopsy schemes often apply more systematic biopsies as well as MRI targeted biopsies. Together, this might have led to an underestimation of the presence of the large cribriform pattern in the current study. Furthermore, treatment modalities have been modified over the years with more common use of active surveillance in low-risk patients who received active treatment two decades ago. Although the large cribriform architecture is believed to have a worse outcome than the small cribriform pattern, there is no consensus on the distinguishing features of large and small cribriform structures. In this study we defined large cribriform pattern as those structures exceeding twice the size of adjacent pre-existent glands, which we also applied in our previous radical prostatectomy study. This threshold is easy to apply, but is subjective. Application of other definitions of the large cribriform pattern, such as an exact-sized cut-off in l m or number of punched-out lumina, will probably result in different distributions and clinical outcomes. Furthermore, interobserver variability on assessment of the cribriform pattern could also affect the outcome of different studies. Finally, we did not perform basal cell immunohistochemistry in each cribriform biopsy to distinguish invasive from intraductal carcinoma, which might have affected definitive grade group assignment in a 31

map_chunks.summary_text: This chunk presents concluding findings on the prognostic significance of cribriform growth patterns in prostate cancer. Both small and large cribriform patterns are independently associated with shorter metastasis-free and disease-specific survival [S1|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17575]. Consequently, men harboring a cribriform growth pattern should not be considered candidates for active surveillance [S2|PMC9321809_HIS-80-1041|17575].
